title: Pointed etale spans descend with both target families fixed
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $B=\varprojlim_i S_i$ and projections $p_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $b\in B$, put $s_i=p_i(b)$, and assume each induced map $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(b)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and affine schemes $P_0,Q_0$ of finite presentation over $S_{i_0}$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $j\geq i_0$ set $P_j=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_j$, $Q_j=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_j$, and put $P_B=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$, $Q_B=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $U$ is affine of finite presentation over $B$, $u\in U$ lies over $b$, and $a:U\to P_B$, $c:U\to Q_B$ are etale $B$-morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing isomorphisms $\kappa(a(u))\to\kappa(u)$ and $\kappa(c(u))\to\kappa(u)$. Then there exist $j\geq i_0$, an affine scheme $U_j$ of finite presentation over $S_j$, etale $S_j$-morphisms $a_j:U_j\to P_j$, $c_j:U_j\to Q_j$, and a $B$-isomorphism $e:U_j\times_{S_j}B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ such that $a\circ e$ and $c\circ e$ are the actual base changes of $a_j$ and $c_j$. Let $u_j$ be the projection of $e^{-1}(u)$, and let $x_j,y_j$ be the images of $a(u),c(u)$ in the fixed models $P_j,Q_j$. Then $a_j(u_j)=x_j$, $c_j(u_j)=y_j$, and the canonical maps $\kappa(x_j)\to\kappa(a(u))$, $\kappa(y_j)\to\kappa(c(u))$, and $\kappa(u_j)\to\kappa(u)$ are isomorphisms. In particular both stage arrows are elementary at $u_j$, meaning their induced residue-field maps are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fixed-family-affine-span-model] to the given $U,a,c$ and the prescribed $P_0,Q_0$. It gives $r\ge i_0$, affine finitely presented $V_r/S_r$, arrows $\alpha_r,\beta_r$ to the actual $P_r,Q_r$, and $e_r:(V_r)_B\cong U$ with $\alpha_{r,B}=a\circ e_r$, $\beta_{r,B}=c\circ e_r$. Set $z=e_r^{-1}(u)$. Because $e_r$ is over $B$, $z$ lies over $b$; the two limit arrows, read through this isomorphism, have exactly the given etaleness and residue-field hypotheses. An isomorphism is an open immersion, hence etale by (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; (2) gives etaleness of the composites with $e_r$. The residue maps are composites with an isomorphism of local rings [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, finite-stage span paragraph; assembly of the two extracted arguments.

proof.text: The prescribed $P_r,Q_r$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and of finite presentation over $S_r$ by (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to $P_0,Q_0$ along $S_r\to S_{i_0}$. Use [lem-trf-finite-stage-span-pointed-etale-refinement] for this supplied span and $z$. Its residue-field hypothesis on the tail $i\ge r$ is part of the original hypothesis. Choose the resulting threshold $k\ge r$, take $j=k$, and put $U_j=V_r\times_{S_r}S_j$. The lemma gives its affineness and finite presentation, both etale arrows, their point-image equalities, and all five canonical residue-field isomorphisms. Let $h_P:(P_r)_j\cong P_j$ and $h_Q:(Q_r)_j\cong Q_j$ be the projection-preserving iterated-pullback comparisons [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $a_j=h_P\circ\alpha_j$ and $c_j=h_Q\circ\beta_j$. These are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], since the comparisons are isomorphisms. Their local-ring isomorphisms also preserve the asserted residue conclusions. Thus the targets remain the prescribed models.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, finite-stage span paragraph; assembly of the two extracted arguments.

proof.text: Let $\theta:(U_j)_B\cong(V_r)_B$ preserve projections and set $e=e_r\circ\theta$. The two projection composites of each base-changed arrow are those of $a\circ e,c\circ e$, so uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the actual-pullback equations. The point $w=\theta^{-1}(z)=e^{-1}(u)$ projects to $u_j$, and the target projections are $x_j,y_j$, giving the required point equations. The three vertical residue maps are the isomorphisms of step 2, composed with the residue isomorphisms of $e,h_P,h_Q$; projection compatibility identifies these with the canonical maps [def-weil-residue-field]. Denote them by $\rho_U,\rho_P,\rho_Q$ and denote the given limit-arrow residue maps by $a^\kappa,c^\kappa$. Functoriality gives $\rho_U\circ a_j^\kappa=a^\kappa\circ\rho_P$ and $\rho_U\circ c_j^\kappa=c^\kappa\circ\rho_Q$. Thus $a_j^\kappa=\rho_U^{-1}\circ a^\kappa\circ\rho_P$ and $c_j^\kappa=\rho_U^{-1}\circ c^\kappa\circ\rho_Q$ are isomorphisms, proving the two elementary-arrow clauses.
